definitions.explanation: A leafy green Chinese vegetable widely used in Japanese and Asian cooking. Has thick white stalks and dark green leaves.

examples.japanese: チンゲン{菜|さい}を{炒|いた}めた。
チンゲン{菜|さい}はクリーム{煮|に}にしてもおいしい。
examples.english: Bok choy is also delicious when stewed in cream.

examples.japanese: スーパーでチンゲン{菜|さい}が{安|やす}かったので、{中華|ちゅうか}スープに{入|い}れることにした。
examples.english: Bok choy was cheap at the supermarket, so I decided to put it in Chinese soup.

notes:
USAGE:
チンゲン{菜|さい} is the standard Japanese name for bok choy, borrowed from the Chinese word. It is one of the most commonly used Chinese vegetables in Japanese cooking. The {菜|さい} suffix means "vegetable."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- チンゲン{菜|さい}の{炒|いた}め{物|もの} (stir-fried bok choy)
- チンゲン{菜|さい}のクリーム{煮|に} (bok choy in cream sauce)
- チンゲン{菜|さい}のおひたし (blanched bok choy with dressing)
